LFunction_ne_zero_right471.twin: Under GRH every nonprincipal Dirichlet L function is nonzero strictly right of one half.
LFunction_ne_zero_right471.instance: q three and s two are allowed. GRH stays an explicit hypothesis.
LFunction_ne_zero_right471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

mellinLine_re_gt_half471.twin: For N greater than one every point on the shifted line has real part greater than one half.
mellinLine_re_gt_half471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

continuous_mellinLine471.twin: The shifted Mellin line is continuous in height for every natural N.
continuous_mellinLine471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

continuous_LFunction_line471.twin: The nonprincipal L function restricted to the shifted line is continuous.
continuous_LFunction_line471.instance: N two and a nonprincipal character modulo three.
continuous_LFunction_line471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

continuous_log_norm_line471.twin: The real logarithm of the modulus is continuous on every nonvanishing shifted line.
continuous_log_norm_line471.instance: N two and a nonprincipal character modulo three. Mathlib nonvanishing applies since the real part exceeds one.
continuous_log_norm_line471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

continuous_lnL_of_slitPlane471.twin: The principal logarithm along the line is continuous when every image point lies in the slit plane.
continuous_lnL_of_slitPlane471.instance: N two and the nonprincipal character modulo four. Its odd supported series stays inside the unit disk about one. No universal slit plane claim is asserted.
continuous_lnL_of_slitPlane471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

norm_log_le_log_norm_add_pi471.twin: The principal logarithm norm is at most the absolute real logarithm of the modulus plus pi.
norm_log_le_log_norm_add_pi471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

norm_LFunction_sub_one471.twin: At real part two every Dirichlet L function is within three quarters of one.
norm_LFunction_sub_one471.instance: The principal character modulo one and s two. The norm difference is pi squared over six minus one.
norm_LFunction_sub_one471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

norm_lnL_anchor471.twin: At real part two the principal logarithm of every Dirichlet L function has norm at most two.
norm_lnL_anchor471.instance: The principal character modulo one and s two.
norm_lnL_anchor471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

log_ball471.twin: A nonvanishing holomorphic function on a positive radius disk has a holomorphic logarithm normalized by the principal value at the center.
log_ball471.instance: f is the exponential, the center is zero and the radius is one. The normalized logarithm is z.
log_ball471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

norm_lnL_disk471.twin: A positive upper bound M for the real logarithm of the modulus on a disk and an anchor logarithm bound A give the Borel Caratheodory norm bound plus pi for the principal logarithm.
norm_lnL_disk471.instance: f is the exponential on the unit disk, M two, A zero and z zero.
norm_lnL_disk471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

lnL_pointwise_of_strip_upper471.twin: Under GRH and the explicit strip upper estimate with coefficient A, log N at least two gives the principal logarithm bound with coefficient twelve A plus eighteen plus pi, uniformly in height and q at most the seventh root of N.
lnL_pointwise_of_strip_upper471.instance: The strip estimate holds with A two by LFunction_strip_log_upper471. N is three to the seventh power and q is three. GRH stays an explicit hypothesis.
lnL_pointwise_of_strip_upper471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

lnL_growth_of_strip_upper471.twin: Under GRH and the strip upper estimate, one positive coefficient and one natural threshold give the cubic logarithmic bound for all heights.
lnL_growth_of_strip_upper471.instance: The strip estimate has coefficient two. The proof chooses threshold max of one and the ceiling of exp two. GRH is not witnessed.
lnL_growth_of_strip_upper471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

character_partial_sum_bound471.twin: For every nonprincipal character modulo q, each partial sum from one through n has norm at most q.
character_partial_sum_bound471.instance: A nonprincipal character modulo three and n three give a complete period with sum zero.
character_partial_sum_bound471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

bounded_mellin_differentiable471.twin: For a measurable real variable coefficient bounded by nonnegative Q on x greater than one, its Mellin integral against x to negative s minus one is holomorphic for positive real part of s.
bounded_mellin_differentiable471.instance: P constantly one and Q one. At s one the integral is one.
bounded_mellin_differentiable471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

LFunction_eq_partial_integral471.twin: For a nonprincipal character and positive real part of s, L equals s times the integral from one to infinity of its partial character sum through floor x times x to negative s minus one.
LFunction_eq_partial_integral471.instance: A nonprincipal character modulo three and s two.
LFunction_eq_partial_integral471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

norm_LFunction_of_partial_integral471.twin: The displayed integral identity and partial sums bounded by q imply norm L at most norm s times q divided by real part s.
norm_LFunction_of_partial_integral471.instance: A nonprincipal character modulo three and s two. Both premises are proved in this file.
norm_LFunction_of_partial_integral471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

log_LFunction_upper_of_norm471.twin: On the closed strip from one half through four, the integral norm bound implies real log modulus at most twice log of q times absolute height plus three.
log_LFunction_upper_of_norm471.instance: A nonprincipal character modulo three and s two. The norm premise follows from the proved integral identity.
log_LFunction_upper_of_norm471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

LFunction_strip_log_upper471.twin: There is an absolute positive coefficient for the one sided logarithmic modulus upper bound on the closed strip from one half through four, for every nonprincipal character.
LFunction_strip_log_upper471.instance: The proof supplies coefficient two. A nonprincipal character modulo three and s two meet the parameters.
LFunction_strip_log_upper471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

principal_log_exp_discontinuous471.twin: The principal logarithm of exp of i t is not continuous at t equal to pi. This audits the claimed nonvanishing justification and does not refute the exact L function leaf.
principal_log_exp_discontinuous471.instance: The exponential is entire and is never zero. At pi the two logarithm limits differ by two pi i.
principal_log_exp_discontinuous471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

exists_continuous_log_path471.twin: A nonvanishing real path with a continuous derivative has a continuous logarithm, normalized at zero by the principal logarithm there.
exists_continuous_log_path471.instance: f and its derivative are exp t. The continuous logarithm is t.
exists_continuous_log_path471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

exists_continuous_lnL_line471.twin: For a nonprincipal character, nonvanishing on the shifted line gives some continuous logarithm there, normalized at height zero. It need not be the principal logarithm at other heights.
exists_continuous_lnL_line471.instance: N two and a nonprincipal character modulo three. Its line lies to the right of one, so Mathlib gives nonvanishing without GRH.
exists_continuous_lnL_line471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

continuous_norm_log471.twin: The norm of the principal logarithm along any nonvanishing continuous path is continuous, including at branch cut crossings.
continuous_norm_log471.instance: f is exp of i t. Its principal logarithm jumps at pi but its norm is continuous there.
continuous_norm_log471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.

intervalIntegrable_lnL_line471.twin: The principal logarithm of the nonprincipal L function on a nonvanishing shifted line is integrable over every compact height interval.
intervalIntegrable_lnL_line471.instance: N two, a nonprincipal character modulo three and the height interval from zero to one. Nonvanishing follows from Mathlib to the right of one.
intervalIntegrable_lnL_line471.source: Standard bridge for P0093 page 159 Section 5. The line itself is on page 156 Lemma 2.
